method: expanding-window pseudo-out-of-sample band evaluation, same origins/seed/draws/paths as coverage_evaluation.json and covid_volatility_evaluation.json; reduced form, levels in model units. sv_* re-run the Carriero-Clark-Marcellino (2016) common stochastic volatility Gibbs sampler (KSC mixture + FFBS for the log-volatility, NIW for (Pi, Sigma | h), IG for sigma2, truncated normal for (c, phi)) on each origin's training sample and simulate the log-volatility forward over the forecast horizon
limitations: lam/mu/theta fixed at the coverage evaluation's defaults (theta off), as in coverage_evaluation.json; the published spec uses theta = 1.
Gaussian log-volatility innovations: a random walk cannot jump to the 2020Q2 variance in one quarter, so without dummies the Covid spike inflates sigma2 and smears into the neighbouring quarters.

The level split between lambda_t and Sigma rests on h_0 = 0 and the IW dummy prior (AR(1) scales from the training sample, Covid-inflated after 2020); the product lambda_t Sigma is what the forecasts use.
100 kept draws per origin (thinned 1 in 10 after 1000 burn-in sweeps); no convergence diagnostics per origin.
Final revised data (pseudo-, not real-time). ~30-49 origins, so 90% coverage has a sampling s.e. of about 0.05.
